name: House — wireframe
notes: A 10 × 7 m house (7 m over all, the garage's wall bands inside it) on a sloped parcel, its ground and first floors pushed 1 m out of the downhill face and the garage 3 m, the driveway cut into the hill and ramped down to the road.

The house is turned 8.06° about its south-east corner to lie parallel to the north-east boundary, 1.5 m off it (D6, D7: 1 m until 2026-11-04, when the site — parcel, relief, road, boundary, the uncle's walls — moved 0.505 m north of the house in this frame).
Heights are metres above the garage-floor datum: real 991.11 m a.s.l. is y 0. The parcel and relief come from the terrain app's survey.

Levels in a terrain profile are finished surfaces; a slab's top is that number, its underside `slab` below; a wall is `wall` thick on the hill side of the line it holds — except the garage's own bands, which lie inside the envelope (z 0–0.3 and 6.7–7) so the house is 7 m over all.

The garage is 6 m clear, x 5.7–11.7 (`x0` 5.7, `extendFront` 1.7), with a 0.30 front wall at x 11.7–12 carrying the 5.00 × 2.25 sectional-door opening under a lintel; the box sits 0.30 further into the hill than the earlier x 6–12 so the clear length and the 3.70 apron both hold. The back 2.7 m of the hill stay in place under the ground floor, so the pit is shallower there and the retaining walls behind it shorter. Inside, along the north wall: a 1.00 stair (z 0.3–1.3) with a railing on its open side, a 0.49 landing inside the door, 19 treads of 0.29 rising 20 × 0.170 to the hall at the back wall line (the 17th riser is the wall), storage under the back 2.25 of the flight, open to the garage, and 5.35 across for two slots (car 2.60 left, quad or second car 2.75 right). The ground and first floors are moved 1 m forward and shortened 2 m at the back, x 3–11, 8 m long (`x0` 3, `extendFront` 1), so the ground floor's slab covers the garage to x 11. A 2 m balcony at ground-floor level (`balcony`, x 11–13) stands in front of the ground floor: its first metre is the garage's roof, its second projects over the garage door. The envelope stays x 0–10: it is the frame the turn and the cut are measured from, not the house's outline.

The apron is what the cut leaves in front of the garage door, so it carries its own `ring` (model frame): the fillet's corner at the garage's front (12, 7), the outer wall's corner (16, 7), the street line north to (16, 5.3), the sweep's chords at its six angle stations through the door's north-jamb point (15.481, 0.77), the corner arc's chords at its twelve to the property line at (11.947, -2.037), the boundary back to the house face (10.25, -1.805) and (8.797, -1.494), the face down to the house's north-east corner (9.02, 0.07), the garage's north edge to its corner (11, −0.21) and the garage's turned face to its south-east corner (11.98, 6.72). Recompute those points if the turn, the garage's depth, the wall or the setback changes.

The street-side retaining wall in front of the apron is one curve (`wallLine` shape 'sweep' on the cut, `onWall` on the wall): on the street line from the ramp's corner (16, 7) north to z 5.3, then a circle of r 20.015 tangent to the street there and passing the point 4.30 m square off the door line at its north jamb (wall included, 4.00 clear; the door's south half is nearer the street, the 4.30 clipped by the road line there), then from that point the corner circle tangent to it, r 3.628, centre (11.947, 1.591), whose lowest point lands on the property line at (11.947, -2.037): there the wall ends square; the apron's north edge along the boundary stays unwalled (a boundary wall was drawn and dropped on 2026-11-04). The street walls are founded 0.5 m under the road. The land between the wall and the street, from z 5.3 to the corner, is taken down to the road's level (`setback` 'road'), all of it on our land: room between our wall and the road for the uncle's sliding gate at his end. The apron `ring` carries the wall as chords at the wall's own stations; regenerate them if the wall changes.

The uncle's entrance: his land is north of the boundary, a platform at about −6.1 (street level) with his wall at the foot of the bank west of it; today that wall kinks out to the old street corner (16, -2.995) because our wall used to stand on the street line, and that kink pinches his entrance. The corner arc gives him the splay on our side. His walls as they stand are `lines` in the neighbour group, transcribed from a sketch on a screenshot (±0.5 m) — measure them on site before setting anything out. The earlier proposal (his wall continuing ours across the boundary on an S, his mouth dug to his platform) was dropped on 2026-11-04.

The yard south of the house is set out on the house's own frame, turned with it: its north edge is the house's south wall (house x 3–11 at z 7), its west and east edges run in line with the house's end walls (house x 3 and x 11) down to the parcel boundary, and the boundary closes it. The east edge reaches the boundary at x 12.54, inside the ramp's uphill wall at 12.7. It is cut down to the ground floor's 0 where the hill stands above it; where the ground lies below, no fill is planned yet — that is decided once the house is built (`fill: true` and a `taper` band on the east edge would add it). Recompute the ring (the four turned points) if the turn or the floors' extent changes.

The house from the plan page (projects/xhevo/house/plan.html, generated by scripts/xhevo-plan-to-scene.mjs): 12 × 7 outside, x 0 to 12, with the glass gable at the front over the garage and no balcony, under one roof (ids rf-*) that starts 3.00 over the ground floor at the side walls and rises at 0.7 per metre to 5.45 at the ridge, 0.40 past the sides and the back, 1.00 past the glass; the side walls stand to the eaves, the back wall and the glass are gables under it; behind the living room's back wall the outer walls start on the fill at 0.8, since there is no house under the bedrooms. Walls 0.30, partitions 0.10. The kitchen is an L in the yard corner, its back wall only as long as the kitchen. The garage flight is an L (ids stair-*): 14 treads up along the north wall from x 9.96, the rest, a 1.1 × 1 landing at -0.85 in the corner at x 4.9 to 5.9, then 4 treads across the house along the living room's back wall and out on the floor beside the bedrooms' flight, 20 risers of 0.17 on 0.29; the rest and the run across sit against the living room's back wall, cut into the hill behind the garage's west wall (that wall cut down to -1.05 there, the back wall carried down to it); its hole from x 8.203 is under a lid 2.2 over every nosing, on the pitch over the run, flat at 1.35 over the rest, 2.03 at the way out. The two bedrooms are half a level up at +1 over the hill end, x 0 to 4.9, on fill (ids gf-fill-*): the hill end is not dug, the soil is made up to 0.8 and their slab sits on it (ids hl-* for the bedrooms). 6 risers of 0.167 climb from the living room against its back wall in the middle of the house, 5 treads of 0.2, 1 long, half of it cut into the fill past the living room's back wall, the last riser being the bedrooms' floor; at the top step the yard bedroom's door in its front wall, and beside it a small hall open to the stair, the north bath's door on its side and the north bedroom's at its end, so the toilet is reached without crossing a bedroom; the 0.50 in front of the yard bedroom's wall beside the flight's upper half is a ledge at +1, open to the living room; the yard bedroom is the whole yard half; the wall between the bedrooms is on the centre line. The slab of the ground level still runs unbroken under the stair hole: levels have no holes.
